verses.text: So get rid of all malice, deceit, hypocrisy, envy, and every kind of slander.
Like newborn babies, crave pure spiritual milk, so that by it you may grow up into salvation,
since you’ve tasted that the Lord is good.
Come to him, the living Stone—rejected by people but chosen and precious to God—
and, like living stones, let yourselves be built into a spiritual house, a holy priesthood, offering spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
For Scripture says: “Look, I lay a chosen and precious cornerstone in Zion, and whoever trusts in him will never be put to shame.”
So, for you who believe, this stone is precious. But for those who don’t believe: “The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone,”
and, “A stone that makes people stumble, a rock that makes them fall.” They stumble because they disobey the word, which is also what they were destined for.
But you are a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, God’s own people, so you can declare the praises of the one who called you out of darkness into his wonderful light.
Once you weren’t a people, but now you’re God’s people. Once you had received no mercy, but now you’ve received mercy.
Dear friends, I urge you, as foreigners and temporary residents, to stay away from sinful desires that wage war against your soul.
Live such good lives among the nations that, though they accuse you of doing wrong, they may see your good deeds and honor God on the day he visits us.
For the Lord’s sake, submit to every human authority, whether to the emperor as the highest authority,
or to governors sent by him to punish wrongdoers and commend those who do right.
For God wants you to silence the ignorance of foolish people by doing good.
Live as free people, but don’t use your freedom to cover up evil. Live as God’s servants.
Honor everyone. Love the family of believers. Fear God. Honor the emperor.
Household servants, submit to your masters with all respect—not only to those who are good and considerate, but also to those who are harsh.
It’s commendable if someone bears up under unjust suffering because they’re conscious of God.
What credit is there in enduring a beating for doing wrong? But if you suffer for doing good and endure it, that’s commendable before God.
You were called to this, because Christ suffered for you and left you an example, so you could follow in his steps.
“He committed no sin, and no deceit was found in his mouth.”
When he was insulted, he didn’t insult back; when he suffered, he didn’t threaten. Instead, he entrusted himself to the one who judges justly.
He himself carried our sins in his body on the cross, so we could die to sins and live for righteousness. By his wounds you’ve been healed.
You were like sheep wandering away, but now you’ve returned to the Shepherd and Guardian of your souls.
